qt: to the Commission Christine Anderson (ESN) Subject:
Limits of service-specific risk assessments under Article 34 DSA – Follow-up to

In its reply to Written Question E-003506/20261, the Commission stated that systemic risk assessments must extend to designated very large online search engines’ algorithmic systems when they are used for other functionalities.. However, despite Article 34(1) of the Digital Services Act2 requiring assessments to be specific to the designated service, the Commission confirmed in P-003415/20263 that ChatGPT’s designation does not cover functionalities which do not qualify as online search engines. 1.

Does Article 34 require the assessment of risks that arise exclusively from nondesignated conversational functionalities, which have no causal connection to the designated search service beyond a shared an algorithmic system? Please answer yes or no.
If so, which specific provision establishes the required connection between such risks and the designated service, notwithstanding the service-specific requirement in Article 34(1)?

If not, what legal criteria determine whether risks arising from a shared algorithmic system can be attributed to the designated search service rather than exclusively to nondesignated functionalities?
